dates.title: Sprint 3 ends

dates.title: Midterm presentation submission
dates.detail: A required, process-focused milestone. You are encouraged to review what the team has built or defined, before or after it, and help correct direction early.

dates.title: Sprint 4
dates.detail: Midterm follow-through, risk correction and showcase readiness.

dates.detail: Final development and testing, demo readiness and rehearsal.

now.title: Separate must-have goals from stretch goals
now.body: Your answers show clear goals were late or are still open. The guide treats scope as a learning contract: the semester needs a must-have outcome, kept apart from stretch goals and future product work.
steps: List the outcomes the team must deliver this semester.
List the nice-to-haves separately.
Review both lists with your PM and record any change.

now.title: Sign the scope document with your PM
now.body: Your answers show the signed scope document was late or is still open. The sponsor representative and the PM sign it, and it was due by the Oct. 8 readiness deadline. It should cover boundaries, objectives, deliverables, assumptions, responsibilities and acceptance expectations.
steps: Ask your PM for the current scope document.
Check that each of those six parts matches your expectations, then sign.
If something blocks signing, tell the PM first, then Capstone leadership.

now.title: Write down requirements and what "done" looks like
now.body: Your answers show written requirements or acceptance criteria were late or are still open. The guide asks sponsors for clear priorities, acceptance expectations, and feedback when user stories or prototypes are reviewed.
steps: For each main deliverable, write one or two sentences on what "done" looks like.
Give them to your PM so they appear in the team's tasks.

now.title: Get data and documents to the team
now.body: Your answers show data or documents were late or are still missing. Students need enough domain context, sample data, documentation or APIs to make progress. Confidential material should travel only through sponsor-approved channels, under your signed agreement and the approved NDA.
steps: List what the team still lacks.
Share it through a channel your organization approves.
If confidentiality is a worry, raise it with Capstone rather than creating a separate NDA.
now.source: Sponsor Guide, sections 3 and 6, and FAQ 15

now.title: Set up accounts, tools and system access
now.body: Your answers show access was late or is still missing. The guide asks sponsors to provide access and environments early enough for students to use them. A sponsor tool such as Slack, Teams or Jira can be used in addition to the official Capstone Discord, but it does not replace it.
steps: Name exactly what the team cannot reach yet.
Grant access, or tell the PM what is blocking it and why.
now.source: Sponsor Guide, sections 3 and 5, and FAQ 4

now.title: Name one representative who can make decisions
now.body: Your answers show a decision-maker was late to be named or still is not. The guide asks for one primary sponsor representative who can make or coordinate timely decisions.
steps: Decide who that is, whether you or a colleague.
Tell your PM their name and how to reach them.

now.title: Name a technical contact for the team
now.body: Your answers show the team got a named technical contact late, or still has none. Students need someone who can answer technical and domain questions. The guide asks sponsors to provide contacts, constraints and decisions early.
steps: Pick someone who can answer the team's technical questions.
Introduce them to the PM and the team.

now.title: Confirm every team member's NDA is complete
now.body: Your answers show the NDA or agreement step was late or is still open. Every Industry team member must complete the required NDA by the announced deadline, and confidentiality and IP follow your executed agreement and the approved NDA.
steps: Ask your PM whether every team member has completed it.
If anything is missing, raise it with the PM and Capstone leadership.
Do not introduce a separate NDA outside the approved process.

now.title: Something is still holding your team up
now.body: You told us the team is still waiting on an item. Start with the PM for routine coordination. For unresolved scope, compliance or program concerns, the guide says to contact Capstone leadership promptly rather than waiting until the Showcase.
steps: Tell the PM exactly what is missing and what you can do about it.
If it is not resolved soon, contact Capstone leadership (see "Who to contact" below).

now.title: Document your scope change with the PM
now.body: You told us the scope changed in a major way without being documented. The guide allows scope changes when needed, but they should be documented with the PM and stay realistic within the five-sprint schedule. Large late expansions are best avoided.
steps: Write a short note on what changed and why.
Send it to the PM so the team's plan and scope document are updated.

now.title: Set up a regular check-in
now.body: You told us there has been little or no regular check-in. The guide strongly prefers weekly check-ins, typically 30 to 60 minutes, with one primary sponsor representative. Weekly or every-two-weeks can work for some projects, but long communication gaps do not.
steps: Pick a recurring slot with your PM.
Use it to review progress, clarify priorities and answer the team's questions.

now.title: Tell Capstone leadership what is not working
now.body: You told us you are not satisfied with how the project got started. The guide says to contact Capstone leadership promptly about unresolved concerns, rather than waiting until the Showcase.
steps: Write down the two or three things that went wrong.
Share them with your PM, and with Capstone leadership if they stay unresolved.

now.title: Weekly check-ins
now.body: Weekly check-ins of about 30 to 60 minutes are strongly preferred, with one primary representative. Weekly or every two weeks can be workable for some projects, but long gaps are not.
steps: Agree a recurring slot with your PM if you do not have one.

now.title: Feedback at sprint reviews and the midterm
now.body: At sprint reviews you review progress, clarify priorities, answer questions and confirm whether user stories and deliverables meet expectations. At the midterm you review what the team has actually built or defined and give corrective feedback.
steps: Before Sun, Nov. 8, look at the team's midterm evidence.
Tell your PM early if direction needs correcting.

now.title: The scope document
now.body: The sponsor representative and the PM sign a scope document that sets boundaries, objectives, deliverables, assumptions, responsibilities and acceptance expectations. It was due by Oct. 8.
steps: Ask your PM to show you the signed copy.

now.title: Must-have goals versus stretch goals
now.body: Keep the must-have outcome for the semester separate from stretch goals and future product work. That keeps the project teachable and achievable.
steps: Check that your PM's plan keeps the two lists apart.

now.title: Raising a concern about a student
now.body: Tell the PM early and describe observable facts, such as a missed meeting, a missed task, an unanswered message or a quality concern. Keep it factual and professional. Do not remove or reassign a student yourself: the PM runs a three-step warning process, and persistent issues go to Capstone leadership.
steps: Report to the PM with specific facts.
Escalate to Capstone leadership only if the issue persists.
now.source: Sponsor Guide, section 7, and FAQ 7 and 8

now.title: Plan for the Final Showcase
now.body: The Showcase is Saturday, Dec. 5, 11:00 AM to 7:00 PM in the NJIT Campus Center Ballroom. All teams are required. Plan to support your team, attend the relevant presentation and judging period, and join sponsor engagement as scheduled.
steps: Put the date in your calendar now.
Watch for the sponsor logistics sent with the event schedule.

now.title: The official Sponsor Evaluation (due Dec. 13)
now.body: The Sponsor Evaluation is a separate component from Showcase judging and counts for 270 of the Industry scorecard's 1,000 base points (27%). Judge what you actually observed: follow-through, professionalism, communication, responsiveness, growth, quality of deliverables, use of feedback, and the value of the outcome. Do not grade only on whether every stretch goal was completed.
steps: Complete the official form by Sun, Dec. 13, 11:59 PM.
This survey is not the Sponsor Evaluation; it is separate.

now.title: Get the Sponsor Partnership Guide & FAQ
now.body: The guide is a sponsor-only companion covering the calendar, scope and readiness rules, communication, how teams are evaluated and a sponsor FAQ. Your signed agreement and the live course schedule take priority if any wording differs.
steps: Ask your PM or your Capstone contact for the current copy.
now.source: Sponsor Guide, front page and section 3

now.title: Check that scope changes are recorded
now.body: Scope changes should go through the PM and be documented, and should stay realistic within the five-sprint schedule.
steps: Ask your PM whether the current scope matches what you expect.

in: Only at sprint reviews or milestones
now.title: Consider a more regular rhythm
now.body: Weekly check-ins are strongly preferred. Every two weeks can work for some projects, but contact only at sprint reviews risks long gaps.
steps: Ask your PM whether a short weekly slot would help the team.

now.title: If the project asks more time than you planned
now.body: The guide expects the Open House, regular check-ins (typically 30 to 60 minutes), milestone feedback, the Showcase and the final evaluation. If you are spending much more than that, tell the PM early so scope or schedule can be adjusted.
steps: Tell your PM what is taking the extra time.
Agree what changes, and document it.
now.source: Sponsor Guide, sections 3 and 5, and FAQ 3

now.title: Good to know as a first-time sponsor
now.body: Capstone is a 3-credit academic course. Students are learners, not employees, and it is not a fee-for-service arrangement. Confidentiality and IP follow your executed agreement and the approved NDA. Any internship or job offer is a separate relationship from the course.
now.source: Sponsor Guide, sections 1 and 3, and FAQ 1, 11 and 12

kit.title: Pre-kickoff checklist
kit.intro: What a sponsor should have ready before the team starts.
steps: Name one primary representative who can make or coordinate timely decisions.
Gather domain context, sample data, documentation, APIs or environments the students will need.
Decide the must-have outcome for the semester, and list stretch goals separately.
Write down priorities and what "done" looks like (acceptance expectations).
Review and sign the current sponsor agreement and any NDA or IP documents.
Plan for the Open House, regular check-ins, milestone feedback, the Showcase and the final Sponsor Evaluation.
Respect student schedules. Do not assume weekend availability beyond the published Capstone events.

kit.title: Scope document template
kit.intro: A starter outline for the document you sign with your PM. Confirm it against the current Capstone scope form.

template.p: What is in scope, and what is clearly out.
The must-have outcome for this semester, and any stretch goals listed separately.
What the team will hand over, in concrete terms.
What must stay true for the plan to work, such as access, data and availability.
Who on the sponsor side and the team side owns what.
How you will decide a deliverable is done.

kit.title: One-page summary of the Sponsor Guide
steps: What it is: a 3-credit academic course. Students are learners, not employees, and it is not fee-for-service.
What you provide: a decision-making representative, enough context, access and data, clear priorities and acceptance expectations, and a project that can adjust to a realistic scope.
How it runs: weekly check-ins (typically 30 to 60 minutes), sprint feedback, a midterm review and the Final Showcase.
How you are involved in grading: the official Sponsor Evaluation is 270 of 1,000 Industry base points (27%), separate from Showcase judging.
Student accountability: students are graded individually. Report concerns early and factually to the PM, and never remove a student yourself.
Confidentiality and IP: your executed agreement and the approved NDA control.

kit.title: "Who to contact when" card
kit.intro: Start with the PM. Go to Capstone leadership promptly for unresolved performance, scope, compliance or program concerns, rather than waiting until the Showcase.

kit.title: Welcome post for your team's Discord channel
kit.intro: A sample message. Replace the brackets. Teams stay reachable in their official Capstone Discord channel; a sponsor's own Slack or Teams can be added alongside it.
kit.sample: Welcome, [team name]! Your sponsor representative is [name]. Your technical contact is [name]. We will check in every [day and time] for about 30 to 60 minutes. Your PM and [name] will sign the scope document by [date]. For access, data or priority questions, post here and tag [name].
